sentences.text: A grey box with a red handle.
You have never run so fast in your life.
Thirty-five seconds of light, then darkness, then silence.
But for thirty-five seconds, you were the brightest, loudest building in town.
House rule: the breaker stays off.
It is too late.
They are not leaning anymore.
They are pushing.
Problem three: the shutter.
It was built to stop one man with a crowbar.
Not 250 people.
By midnight, the steel has started to bow.
So you build a second wall.
Pallets of bottled water, a ton each, parked against the steel.
Then shopping carts, nested and chained, thirty to a row.
One row weighs as much as a small car.
But a wall only buys time.
You need them to leave.
Aisle 9 sells alarm clocks, the loud kind with two bells.
You set one for noon.
Then, in the dark, you hurl it off the back of the roof as far as you can.
At noon it starts ringing, and 250 heads swing the other way.
